newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens buys stake in Canada's Broadband Networks.
newsitem.headline: Siemens buys stake in Canada's Broadband Networks.

text.p: German industrial giant Siemens AG said Saturday it bought 5 percent of Canada's Broadband Networks Inc. as part of a joint research project aimed at developing wireless video and data networks.

Under the agreement, which included an option for Siemens to buy another 5 percent of BNI, the two companies hope to develop technology for carrying digital television, Internet access and interactive video over wireless networks.
Today's wireless networks do not operate with the speed or the bandwidth required to transmit high-quality digital TV, or to link computer users to the Internet.
The two companies plan to work with Newbridge Networks, a Siemens partner in high-speed network technology and holder of a 15 percent stake in BNI.
The move is the latest in a series of investments Siemens has made to bolster its position in North America and in emerging technology markets.

In January, the company took over keyless car lock maker Huelsbeck & Fuerst GmbH, a German company with two U.S. plants that supply Ford Motor Co. and General Motors Corp. It also acquired Texas-based AEG Electrocom International Inc., a $650 million producer of postal sorting equipment.

Those deals came four months after its U.S. communications unit bought a 20 percent stake in Internet specialist Persimmon IT Inc. of Durham, N.C. In February 1996, Siemens formed an alliance with Newbridge, a leading developer of high-speed networks.
